author: Latin Business Daily
title: Minister Daniel Mas meets with municipal associations to address local development challenges
text:
Minister Daniel Mas meets with municipal associations to address local development challenges
Minister of Economy, Development and Tourism and Mining, Daniel Mas, met with the leadership of the Chilean Association of Municipalities (ACHM) and the Association of Rural Municipalities (AMUR) on June 16 to coordinate efforts between the Ministry of Economy, the Undersecretariat for Regional and Administrative Development, and municipalities across Chile. The meeting was attended by various municipal authorities including Karina Delfino Mussa, first vice president of ACHM and mayor of Quinta Normal; Juan Pablo Olave Cambara, second vice president of ACHM and mayor of Isla de Maipo; Felipe Muñoz Heredia, first vice president of AMUR and mayor of Padre Hurtado; Isabel Valenzuela, mayor of Colina; among other representatives.
The discussions focused on key challenges faced by municipalities in communal development. Authorities emphasized coordination between central government and local officials. Special attention was given to modernizing the General Urban Planning and Construction Ordinance (OGUC).
Mas highlighted the urgency for joint work with municipalities as essential actors in addressing housing needs. He said there is a need to create 400,000 new social housing units during this administration because more than one and a half million people require housing. "We have to seek positions that add up because one problem we have is the housing deficit since at least 650,000 families do not have homes and 120,000 families are living in camps," said Mas.
Undersecretary Karlfranz Koehler said, "The proposal for changes to the General Ordinance being studied goes in the right direction because it contains incentives for building new homes. It will allow municipalities to collect more income through building permit payments, property tax collection under real estate contributions law, as well as through public space contribution law. It is a very good opportunity to attract investments into municipalities." He also stressed that each municipality faces unique realities requiring tailored solutions: "In this context we want to invite everyone to build agreements based on facts so that progress can be made together."
Felipe Muñoz Heredia said, "We are going to raise what difficulties we see as mayors but also understanding this is part of reconstruction plans—especially economically—to generate more housing which is our goal from both association level and Housing Commission." Miguel Araya added, "This meeting clarifies many doubts we have as a rural municipality... I agree that any counterproposal should be made jointly so we can build together the city our country needs." Jessica Mualim concluded, "A meeting like this brings dialogue closer between central government levels and local governments seeking joint solutions long awaited by thousands in our commune regionally—and nationally."
The meeting ended with a commitment from all parties involved—the Ministry of Economy, Undersecretariat for Regional Development, ACHM and AMUR—to maintain ongoing collaborative work aimed at advancing measures supporting local economic development while recognizing each municipality's specific needs.
